title: Weather, Climate & Disaster Overlay Library
source_and_design_basis: ENV-04_OVERLAY_MODEL_v1.0.0.json definition, relation, intensity, effect-key and deterministic-resolution contract
ENV-05 through ENV-10 preset trait/hint records that deferred weather, hydrology, ecological and geologic conditions
library_rules: An overlay is a reusable environmental delta, never a base environment identity.
No overlay automatically activates another overlay. Causal chains remain GM/runtime/event authority unless separately authored later.
Relations apply only when both referenced overlays are active in materially overlapping scopes.
Intensity uses ENV-04 canonical bands only where a local/content mapping exists; no cross-phenomenon numeric comparison is implied.
Semantic deltas define environment-state effects without inventing universal movement, damage, endurance, exposure or structural formulas.
Stable effect keys permit equivalent contributions to deduplicate while unrelated effects from the same overlay remain active.
All definitions are owner-authorized content design, not claims of recovered source text.

overlays.name: Heavy Rain
overlays.applicability: Requires an atmosphere/medium capable of liquid precipitation; unsupported where the resolved environment cannot sustain rain.

deltas.value_or_reference: visibility reduced by dense rainfall according to local intensity
elevated surface runoff and water input
wet, slick, muddy or waterlogged route complications where substrate permits
rain exposure increases value of cover and drainage

overlays.name: Monsoon Regime
overlays.applicability: Represents an active seasonal monsoon regime, not a permanent climate identity; stable climate classification remains preset/local parameterization.

deltas.value_or_reference: monsoon-season water input and drainage pressure
seasonally reduced route reliability where drainage and substrate are vulnerable
seasonal surface-water availability may increase where locally supported

overlays.name: Fog
overlays.applicability: Requires a medium and local conditions capable of suspended condensate or equivalent ordinary fog.

deltas.value_or_reference: distance and detail visibility reduced by fog
visual navigation references become less reliable
visual discovery and approach context is obscured

overlays.name: Thunderstorm
overlays.applicability: Requires an atmosphere/medium capable of ordinary convective storm behavior; rainfall may be represented separately when materially relevant.

deltas.value_or_reference: lightning/electrical strike hazard present
rapid light and visibility changes from cloud, rain bands and lightning
gusts and storm cells complicate exposed movement

overlays.name: Heavy Snow
overlays.applicability: Requires conditions capable of frozen precipitation; thermal enabling conditions may come from the base environment or ENV-12/local state.

deltas.value_or_reference: snow accumulation alters exposed surface condition
visibility reduced by dense snowfall
snow cover obscures routes and complicates travel according to accumulation

overlays.name: Blizzard
overlays.applicability: Requires snow available for active snowfall or wind-driven transport plus strong wind; thermal enabling conditions are external/base or ENV-12.

deltas.value_or_reference: wind-driven snowfall/drift accumulation
severe snow/wind obscuration including whiteout where intensity supports
high wind complicates exposed movement and route keeping
combined wind and snow increase shelter dependence

relations.scope: same materially overlapping scope while blizzard is active
relations.note: Duplicate snowfall/visibility contributions resolve through the blizzard; unrelated accumulated-snow consequences may remain in local/runtime state.

overlays.name: Windstorm / Gale
overlays.applicability: Requires a medium capable of significant wind or analogous ordinary atmospheric flow.

deltas.value_or_reference: exposed travel, balance and route choice complicated by high wind
windborne debris/falling-object hazard where material is available
exposed water surfaces become wind-driven/rough where applicable

overlays.name: Hurricane / Cyclone
overlays.applicability: Requires an ordinary atmosphere and storm context capable of a large rotating cyclone; local land/ocean context determines individual effects.

intensity.note: ENV bands are semantic unless a local source supplies another mapped scale.

deltas.value_or_reference: widespread severe wind complicates exposed movement
rain bands and spray reduce visibility
large storm rainfall can add substantial runoff where precipitation reaches the scope
widespread debris/falling-object hazard

relations.note: Generic high-wind contributions are subsumed; unique local gale context may remain outside the cyclone scope.
If storm surge is separately active, cyclone wind/pressure context can increase surge severity; no surge is auto-created.

overlays.name: Tornado
overlays.applicability: Requires an atmosphere and storm context capable of a localized rotating vortex.

deltas.value_or_reference: localized extreme wind makes exposed movement highly unstable
localized high-energy debris hazard
ordinary shelter may be inadequate within the vortex path depending on construction

relations.note: Generic wind complication is subsumed within the vortex path.

overlays.name: Sandstorm / Dust Storm
overlays.applicability: Requires loose sand/dust/particulate material and sufficient wind; not limited to desert presets if local material is present.

deltas.value_or_reference: visibility reduced by airborne sand/dust
airborne mineral particulate load elevated
route finding and landmark use complicated by particulate obscuration
abrasive particulate exposure where unprotected

overlays.name: Hailstorm
overlays.applicability: Requires atmospheric storm conditions capable of hail formation.

deltas.value_or_reference: falling hail impact hazard according to local intensity
temporary hail accumulation may alter exposed surfaces
exposed vegetation/crops may be damaged where locally applicable

overlays.name: Flood
overlays.applicability: Requires a water source or local condition capable of inundating normally exposed terrain/structures; baseline floodplain or Flooded Forest identity alone does not mean this overlay is active.

deltas.value_or_reference: water occupies normally exposed terrain/structures according to local depth/extent
routes, crossings and ground travel are altered by standing/moving floodwater
low-lying shelter/access may be lost or degraded
stored/local resources may become inaccessible, damaged or contaminated as locally supported

overlays.name: Flash Flood
overlays.applicability: Requires terrain/drainage capable of rapid concentrated flow; especially relevant to channels, canyons, washes, steep catchments and constrained urban drainage.

deltas.value_or_reference: rapid temporary inundation along affected flow paths
fast-moving floodwater/torrent condition
crossings/routes may become abruptly impassable or hazardous
debris/scour/impact hazards may accompany rapid flow

relations.note: Shared inundation contributions deduplicate while Flash Flood retains high-velocity flow; the result is a derived combined flood state, not a new durable overlay identity.

overlays.name: Drought
overlays.applicability: Represents sustained water deficit relative to a local baseline; arid presets do not automatically imply Drought.

deltas.value_or_reference: surface/accessible water availability reduced relative to local baseline
soils/vegetation/fuels become unusually dry where applicable
water-dependent local resources become less reliable

relations.note: If Wildfire is separately active, drought-dried fuels can increase spread/persistence; no fire is auto-created.

overlays.name: Storm Surge
overlays.applicability: Requires a coast, shore, estuary, large open-water margin or other water body capable of wind/pressure-driven level rise.

deltas.value_or_reference: temporary wind/pressure-driven water-level rise
surge-associated wave/current energy elevated
coastal/shore routes and access points may flood or become wave-swept

overlays.name: Tsunami / Seiche
overlays.applicability: Requires a sufficiently large water body and a separately established triggering context; ENV-11 does not auto-create the trigger.

deltas.value_or_reference: large transient displacement/oscillation raises and withdraws water levels
high-energy surge/wave/current condition
debris/scour/impact hazard accompanies inundation where material is present
shoreline, harbor and low-route access may change abruptly

overlays.name: Wildfire
overlays.applicability: Requires burnable fuel and conditions supporting combustion; grassland, forest, savanna or drought does not automatically imply active Wildfire.

deltas.value_or_reference: active flame/heat/fire-front hazard present where burning
smoke and combustion particulate load elevated downwind/within affected scope
smoke can obscure visibility
active fire, heat, smoke and falling material can close or redirect routes
exposed biological/material resources may be consumed or damaged

overlays.name: Volcanic Ash
overlays.applicability: May occur near or far from an eruption where airborne ash is established; does not require the Volcanic Eruption overlay to remain active.

deltas.value_or_reference: volcanic particulate load elevated
airborne ash reduces visibility and light penetration
ash accumulates on exposed surfaces according to local intensity
exposed water/food/material resources may be fouled by ash

overlays.name: Volcanic Eruption
overlays.applicability: Requires a separately established active volcanic/geothermal source; a Volcano preset does not automatically mean eruption.

deltas.value_or_reference: active eruptive hazards such as lava, pyroclastic, ballistic, vent or ground-instability phenomena as locally established
terrain can be altered/blocked by eruptive deposits or flows where present
routes can be blocked or redirected by active eruptive zones

relations.note: If Volcanic Ash is separately active, eruption can increase ash production/intensity; eruption does not auto-create a separate ash overlay.

overlays.name: Earthquake
overlays.applicability: Requires a separately established seismic/tectonic or analogous ordinary physical cause; no supernatural cause is inferred.

deltas.value_or_reference: ground motion and local surface disruption present according to intensity
routes/crossings/structures may become unstable or blocked as locally supported
falling-object/structural-collapse hazard where built or unstable material exists

relations.note: If Landslide is separately active, seismic ground motion can increase instability; no landslide is auto-created.

overlays.name: Avalanche
overlays.applicability: Requires a slope and unstable snow/ice/debris mantle capable of rapid downslope movement; Highland/Ice Mass alone does not imply an active avalanche.

deltas.value_or_reference: rapid downslope snow/ice/debris burial and impact hazard
routes/crossings may be buried, cut or redirected
fresh avalanche debris/deposit alters local surface

overlays.name: Landslide / Mudslide
overlays.applicability: Requires a slope/bank/cut/fill or other unstable material capable of downslope movement; heavy rain or earthquake may contribute only when separately active/established.

deltas.value_or_reference: rapid soil/rock/debris movement, burial and impact hazard
routes, channels and access points may be blocked or redirected
fresh slide/debris deposits alter local terrain
slides may block/divert channels where they intersect watercourses

authored_cross_overlay_relations.note: When both are active, monsoon regime increases persistence/recurrence context; it does not auto-create a heavy-rain event.
When both are active, rainfall can add runoff/water input; it does not auto-create Flood.
When both are active on susceptible terrain, saturation can increase slope instability; it does not auto-create Landslide.
When rain reaches burning fuels, it can reduce exposed fire spread/persistence; it never guarantees extinguishment and does not suppress unrelated smoke/damage effects.
Cyclone wind/pressure can increase separately active surge severity.
Dry fuels can increase separately active wildfire spread/persistence.
An ash-producing eruption can increase separately represented ashfall.
Seismic ground motion can increase a separately active slope failure.

explicit_non_causation_examples: Heavy Rain does not automatically activate Flood or Flash Flood.
Monsoon Regime does not automatically activate Heavy Rain at every moment.
Thunderstorm does not automatically activate Heavy Rain or Hailstorm.
Hurricane/Cyclone does not automatically activate Storm Surge, Flood or Tornado.
Drought does not automatically activate Wildfire.
Earthquake does not automatically activate Landslide or Tsunami/Seiche.
Volcanic Eruption does not automatically activate the separate Volcanic Ash overlay.
Blizzard does not automatically activate Avalanche.
